subject.title: Install ClawHub packages for new Claw agents

question: Should experimental `claws add` be permitted to install or reuse a process-wide plugin using only the displayed plan-integrity consent, or must shared plugins require a separate host-level authorization model?
rationale: This is a product and security-boundary choice: plugins execute in the shared runtime, while the PR intentionally does not provide per-agent isolation or a separate host grant.

options.title: Require explicit host authorization
options.body: Keep package planning but require a clearly separate host-level approval before any shared-plugin mutation or reuse is accepted.

options.title: Limit this stage to skills
options.body: Land only workspace-scoped skill lifecycle support and defer shared-plugin mutation until the host authorization contract is designed.

options.title: Accept exact-plan consent as host consent
options.body: Treat the operator's exact `claws add --yes --plan-integrity` approval as sufficient authorization for the disclosed process-wide plugin action.

recommendation.title: Require explicit host authorization
recommendation.body: Keep package planning but require a clearly separate host-level approval before any shared-plugin mutation or reuse is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review comment directly frames the shared-host/plugin-isolation policy decision that remains unresolved.
